findingsInProgress.claim: Findings 1 (Travis footprint acquisition gap) and 3 (no-ring parcels) share one root cause for Travis, and it is a real source-data absence, not a join failure.

evidence.instrument: SELECT county_fips, count(*) FROM tx_building_footprint WHERE county_fips IN (six CTX-D counties) GROUP BY 1
atoms WHERE entity_type='building-footprint' AND parcelNodeId LIKE '48453:%', split by body ? 'absence'
evidence.result: 72,919 real (non-absence) atoms, 323,543 declared-absence atoms (kind=no-footprint-feature). 72,919 matches the dispatch's cited atom count exactly.

evidence.instrument: Exported (bash comm/sort) three Travis id sets: cad_property distinct prop_id (500,307, exact dispatch match), tier1 envelope-null place_key (119,389, exact dispatch match), building-footprint-atom-touched parcelNodeId (380,917)
evidence.result: comm -12 (untouched-by-footprint-writer) vs (no-ring) = 119,389 of 119,390; comm -23 the other direction = 0. The no-ring set and the footprint-writer-silently-skipped set are the same set, up to one outlier.

evidence.instrument: SQL join (inline VALUES array, read-only role) of the 119,389 no-ring Travis prop_ids against txgio_parcel(county_fips='48453')
evidence.result: 0 have a row in txgio_parcel at all (not a null-geom row, not a join-key mismatch -- absent from the source table entirely). property_use_code breakdown of the 119,389: A4 (condo) 53,672 (45%), blank 39,138 (33%), M1 (mobile home) 11,684 (10%), remainder scattered (O1/C1/F4/etc).

evidence.instrument: Same envelope-null / txgio-presence check for McLennan (48309)
evidence.result: 0 no-ring rows (exact dispatch match) and txgio_parcel distinct prop_id (114,255) equals cad_property distinct prop_id (114,255) exactly -- a real, non-vacuous full-coverage county. McLennan's cad_property carries only 2 A4 and 2 M1 rows out of 114,255 -- negligible condo/mobile-home population explains the zero.

findingsInProgress.interpretation: The footprint writer and the tier1 envelope builder both correctly cannot produce a ring/footprint for a parcel txgio_parcel never received a polygon for. The real defect is that the footprint writer's silent-skip (no atom at all, not even a declared absence) for these 119,389 Travis parcels is itself the SILENT FALLBACK class DEV_PROCESS section 0 and AGENT_CONTRACT section 5 name explicitly -- parcel-node's own three absence kinds (no-parcel-geometry / geometry-incomplete / parcel-key-unresolved) already model exactly this state; building-footprint has no equivalent for 'CAD parcel has no ring at all', so it says nothing rather than declining honestly.
findingsInProgress.secondMechanismConsidered: A join-key mismatch between cad_property.prop_id and txgio_parcel.prop_id (e.g. leading-zero or format drift) was considered and rejected: the inline-VALUES join used the exact prop_id string with no normalization and found true absence (0 rows), not a near-miss; separately, cad_property_vintage_crosswalk has 0 rows for Travis, ruling out an un-applied vintage remap as the explanation.

LESSON: the two Neon databases behind this lane's data (CORTEX_DATABASE_URL -> neondb; ATOMS_DATABASE_URL -> hauska_mcp) are genuinely separate instances -- no cross-database SQL join is possible; set reconciliation across them requires exporting id lists and diffing client-side (used comm/sort here on <1M-row sets, fast enough not to need a heavier approach).

LESSON: CORTEX_DATABASE_URL connects as a role that refuses CREATE TABLE ('cannot execute CREATE TABLE in a read-only transaction') -- confirmed read-only at the connection level, not just by convention. Cross-referencing a large id list against it requires an inline unnest(ARRAY[...]) VALUES clause via a generated .sql file, not a temp table.
